title: Chinese EV import quota: second-period administration
fact: For the second period of quota year 1, 24,500 vehicles plus unused first-period volume are available, and the quota is administered first-come, first-served until further notice.
analysis: The later notice governs current administration and should be used instead of the April consultation for operating rules.
limit: This describes administration, not utilization, price effects, investment effects, or future allocation policy.
source: Global Affairs Canada, Notice to Importers No. 1168
passage: The total available quantity for the 2nd Period of Quota Year 1 will be 24,500 vehicles plus any unused volumes from the 1st Period.

title: Chinese EV quota: initial implementation and consultation
fact: The first-year annual quota was set at 49,000 vehicles and initially implemented on 1 March 2026 for six months.
analysis: This record establishes the initial quota and consultation context.
limit: Use EV-CC-01 for operating rules beginning 1 September 2026.
passage: The quota volume for the first year is 49,000 vehicles.

title: Section 301 strategic tariff modifications
fact: USTR finalized additional or increased Section 301 duties on selected strategic Chinese products in September 2024.
analysis: The U.S. instrument differs in legal authority and product coverage from Canada's EV quota.
limit: Current combined duty treatment requires product-level tariff verification.
source: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative
passage: The U.S. Trade Representative determined to impose additional Section 301 duties or increase existing duties on certain products of China.

title: Integrated automotive production context
fact: More than 90% of Canadian-made vehicles and 60% of Canadian-made auto parts were reported as exported to the United States.
analysis: U.S. market access remains important context for Canadian automotive choices.
limit: This is context, not a directly comparable quota or tariff instrument.
passage: More than 90% of Canadian-made vehicles and 60% of Canadian-made auto parts are exported to the United States.

title: Northern-border fentanyl seizure context
fact: Between September 2025 and August 2026, U.S. CBP attributed 4.85 lb of fentanyl seizures to the Northern Border and 10,216 lb to the Southern Border; the Northern Border represented approximately 0.1% of the cited border-enforcement total.
analysis: The statistic provides enforcement-seizure context for the Canada-U.S. border.
limit: This is a share of recorded seizures, not an estimate of trafficking, production origin, or policy effectiveness.
passage: Northern Border seizures accounted for approximately 0.1% of total U.S. fentanyl seizures by U.S. border enforcement.

title: Fentanyl precursor supply-chain assessment
fact: DEA's 2025 assessment describes Mexican cartels producing fentanyl using precursor chemicals and pill presses sourced from companies in China.
analysis: The evidence describes a multi-country criminal supply chain rather than a direct-China-only flow.
limit: The assessment is not a complete measure of every trafficking route.
passage: DEA describes Mexican cartels producing fentanyl using precursor chemicals and pill presses sourced from companies in China.

title: Agricultural tariff changes
fact: China suspended selected tariffs through the end of 2026 and reduced the combined applied tariff on Canadian canola seed to 14.9%.
analysis: The measures partially restored market access after the 2025 deterioration.
limit: The announcement does not establish realized shipment or producer-income effects.
passage: Effective March 1, 2026, China suspended specified tariffs and reduced tariffs on Canadian canola seed to a combined applied tariff rate of 14.9%.

title: 2025 bilateral hydrocarbon trade
fact: In 2025 Canada exported C$157.5 billion and imported C$34.4 billion in specified hydrocarbons with the United States.
analysis: Infrastructure and geography give the U.S. relationship structural importance for Canadian energy choices.
limit: The values cover specified hydrocarbons, not all energy.
passage: Exports of crude oil, RPPs, natural gas, and NGLs to the U.S. totaled $157.5 billion in 2025.

title: Canada-China Financial Working Group
fact: Canada and China launched a Financial Working Group covering policy, markets, stability, regulation, anti-money laundering, capital flows, and global financial governance.
analysis: The group establishes dialogue, not commercial market access by itself.
limit: Future meetings and implementation outcomes require separate evidence.
passage: The FWG provides a structured and technical channel to enhance bilateral engagement on financial issues.

title: Indo-Pacific strategic context
fact: Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy provides a long-term framework for regional engagement, including security and resilience objectives.
analysis: Regional strategy should be separated from specific operational measures.
limit: An earlier implementation update is not a complete 2026 status report.
passage: The strategy provides a framework for regional engagement.
